## Tear off tabs

- Drag a tab out of every window and drop it to open it, still connected, in a new window under the pointer. Dragging a window's only tab moves the window instead of leaving an empty one behind.
- The pointer shows the move cursor while a tab is outside the windows, and Escape still cancels the drag.

## Agents in the terminal

- An agent's transcript is no longer read as shell commands. While an agent is running, its messages and prompt-shaped lines aren't recorded as commands or reported as running, and the ruler hides until the shell is back.
- oh-my-pi's π mark is dropped from tab titles along with its spinner; the tab's agent icon already shows which agent it is.

## Tabs and sessions stay consistent

- Unpinning a tab no longer leaves an ordinary tab in front of a pinned one.
- Closing the focused pane moves focus and the ruler highlight to the pane left behind.
- Switching workspaces no longer clears the unseen-output marks on background tabs.
- A sessions file from an older build that holds two sessions with the same ID loads again, keeping the first of each, instead of leaving you with no sessions.
- A local shell only starts once Windows has placed it in its process job, so it can't outlive Resesh.
- Renaming tabs, searching sessions and changing selection in background panes no longer redo work across every session and tab.

Choose the x64 download for Intel or AMD PCs. Choose ARM64 only for Windows on ARM devices.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/bpbp-boop/resesh/compare/v0.28.0...v0.29.0)
